topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens, testing methodologies, and tumor initiators versus promoters.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Environmental Exposures, and the Bad Luck Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, exploring the interplay between intrinsic random mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents and Mechanisms of Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific biological, chemical, and physical agents, detailing the biochemical and cellular mechanisms through which pathogens, radiation, and metabolically activated compounds cause direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Initiator–Promoter Dynamics, and Host Susceptibility

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure patterns and test the mutagenic potential of compounds.

topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing key takeaways on environmental carcinogenesis and discussing everyday risk-versus-benefit trade-offs.
